deep.reconstruction:
Context (§§473–476, previous page): p = 10p'+1 is prime; I write P for the prime and p for Euler's parameter, so P = 10p+1. Suppose a, b, c, d, e are distinct residues mod P (each < P) with a^5 ≡ b^5 ≡ c^5 ≡ d^5 ≡ e^5 (mod P). Euler takes successive divided differences of f(x) = x^5. Each division is by a difference of distinct numbers < P, which is nonzero mod P; this justification is my addition. The steps are:
- (§474) (x^5 − a^5)/(x − a) = h_4(a,x) ≡ 0 for x = b, c, d, e.
- (§475) Subtracting the b-expression from the c, d, e ones and dividing by c−b, d−b, e−b gives h_3(a,b,x) ≡ 0 for x = c, d, e.
- (§476, top of this page) Subtracting again and dividing by d−c, e−c gives h_2(a,b,c,x) ≡ 0 for x = d, e. Explicitly: c²+cd+d²+bc+bd+b²+ac+ad+ab+a² ≡ 0, and the same with e in place of d.
- One more difference, divided by d−e, gives h_1 = a+b+c+d+e ≡ 0 (mod P).
Here h_k is the complete homogeneous symmetric polynomial. In modern terms this is the 4th divided difference of x^5 at five nodes, equivalently Vieta: the x^4-coefficient of x^5 − r is 0.

§477: So any five numbers with equal fifth-power residues sum to a multiple of P. Five distinct numbers in [1, P−1] have sum between 15 and 5P−15. Hence the sum is P, 2P, 3P or 4P.

§478: Allowing negative residues, a+b+c+d+e ≡ 0, so e ≡ −(a+b+c+d) is uniquely determined by the other four. Hence at most five numbers share a given fifth-power residue. In modern terms, x^5 ≡ r has at most 5 roots mod a prime; this is a special case of Lagrange's theorem.

§479: This gives a 'new proof' of the count of fifth-power residues mod a prime 2q+1:
- If 5 ∤ q, it is 2q (all nonzero numbers are residues).
- If q = 5p, it is 2q/5 (only a fifth are residues).
The second case also uses §§472–473: not every number is a residue, and one residue has five roots. The full coset structure (each residue has exactly 5 roots, namely b·{1, a, a², a³, a⁴}) is only made explicit on the next page (§486).

§480: For P = 10p+1 there are 2p residues. Since (−x)^5 = −x^5, they are closed under negation, so the count is even. Each residue arises from exactly five bases.

§§481–482: Tables of the fifth-power residues for P = 11 and 31. Each row gives a residue r, its five fifth roots, and the four non-residue classes 2r, 4r, 8r, 16r mod P.
- For P = 11: residues {1, 10}. Roots of 1 are {1, 3, 4, 5, 9}; roots of 10 are {2, 6, 7, 8, 10}. Classes are 2,4,8,5 and 9,7,3,6.
- For P = 31: residues {1, 5, 26, 6, 25, 30}, each with its five roots. The four classes 2R, 4R, 8R, 16R together with R partition 1..30.

§483 begins the P = 41 table, which continues on the next page.
errors: No numerical errors: every entry of the tables for 11 and 31 checks (roots, residues, and classes 2r, 4r, 8r, 16r mod P). Each row's five roots sum to a multiple of P (e.g. 7+14+19+25+28 = 93 = 3·31), as §477 predicts.

Logical gap (minor): §§478–479 prove only 'at most 5 roots per residue'. Concluding that the count is exactly 2q/5 needs every residue to have exactly 5 roots, i.e. the coset structure b·{a^k}, which is supplied only later in §486. Alternatively it rests on §473's assertion, which itself depends on earlier chapters. The step from 'at most five' to 'number of residues = 2p' is not fully justified on this page.
The divisions by d−e, c−d, etc. silently require the five numbers to be pairwise distinct mod P. This is implicit but correct.

results.what: If a^5≡b^5≡c^5≡d^5≡e^5 (mod P) with a,…,e distinct, then the successive divided differences h_4, h_3, h_2 and finally a+b+c+d+e vanish mod P
results.modern_name: Divided differences of x^n / complete homogeneous symmetric polynomials; equivalently Vieta (sum of roots of x^5 − r is 0)
results.usually_credited_to: Newton (divided differences); the root-sum relation is Vieta/Girard

results.what: x^5 ≡ r (mod prime) has at most 5 solutions
results.modern_name: Lagrange's theorem on polynomial congruences (special case x^n − r)
results.usually_credited_to: Lagrange 1768 (general); Euler had the binomial case in E262 (1761) and the Tractatus

results.what: Number of fifth-power residues mod prime 2q+1 is 2q if 5∤q and 2q/5 if 5|q; residues closed under negation
results.modern_name: Count of n-th power residues = (P−1)/gcd(n, P−1)

results.what: Tables of fifth-power residues, roots and non-residue cosets mod 11 and 31
results.modern_name: Coset decomposition of (Z/P)^* modulo the subgroup of fifth powers

deep.surprise_reason: This is part of Euler's Tractatus de numerorum doctrina (E792, published 1849), whose power-residue theory parallels his published E262/E449. The divided-difference proof of 'at most n roots' is a known Euler technique, and the tables are routine and correct.

checkable.sympy: all(pow(x,5,11) == (1 if x in [1,3,4,5,9] else 10) for x in range(1,11))
checkable.asserts: Fifth powers mod 11 are 1 exactly for x in {1,3,4,5,9}, else 10
Euler's table of fifth roots mod 31 is correct
Non-residue classes mod 31 are the cosets 2R, 4R, 8R, 16R

checkable.asserts: The five fifth roots of each residue sum to 0 mod P (§477)

checkable.asserts: Number of fifth-power residues is 2q or 2q/5 (§479)
